ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are moving to dramatically expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, seeking to add more than 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings revealed the AI was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development signals a significant escalation in one of the music industry's most closely watched AI copyright cases.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The move mirrors parallel action against Suno and reflects a broader industry push to hold AI music platforms accountable for training data practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors pursuing a copyright case over Meta's Llama AI model have moved to sue Meta's AI scientists directly, a legal strategy that could expose individual researchers to personal liability for decisions made during AI training. The case raises significant questions about where copyright responsibility sits within AI development teams.

ip_top_stories.title: MiniMax loses bid to dismiss Disney copyright lawsuit over AI system
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has rejected Chinese AI company MiniMax's attempt to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros., allowing the case to proceed. The ruling keeps alive a significant test of whether AI systems that reproduce copyrighted content can be held liable under US copyright law.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The decision marks a notable moment for awards bodies in the publishing and comics world grappling with how to handle AI-assisted works. [Metered]

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal action over voice rights is prompting wider debate about whether AI-generated vocal likenesses can be protected under existing copyright and related rights frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulations to address AI systems that summarise news content without compensation, responding to concerns from media organisations about revenue loss.

ip_further_links.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Media organisations in Australia are opposing government moves that would ease copyright protections in relation to AI training, arguing the changes would harm the creative sector.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With US federal policy on AI-generated work ownership stalled, individual states are beginning to introduce their own legislation to fill the gap.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions - Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA)
ip_further_links.summary: CEPA argues that Europe's existing copyright framework is hampering AI development on the continent, creating a competitive disadvantage relative to jurisdictions with more permissive rules.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis suggests that mounting copyright litigation and unresolved IP liability risks could significantly constrain investment in and adoption of generative AI technologies.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI-assisted research is transforming user behaviour and what this means for the future of scholarly publishing models.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creatives urge the government to 'hold the line' on AI and copyright law
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative sector representatives are calling on the government to resist pressure to loosen copyright protections in ways that would benefit AI companies at the expense of human creators.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated agency to collect and distribute AI-related royalties to creators, as part of broader efforts to modernise its copyright framework for the digital age.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is taking an active role in shaping national and European policy on AI and copyright, positioning itself as a model for how rights management organisations can respond to generative AI.
